gate_traps.note: Hennessy really did activate (Hennessy Social Club, 2026-05-09 recap). Tests that the gate distinguishes property-wide sponsorship from 21+-zone activation; a naive 'revealed preference = OK' would wave it through.

codes.name: Beer Institute Advertising and Marketing Code
codes.threshold: 73.6% of audience of legal drinking age (21+) for magazines, newspapers, TV, radio and digital placements (since 2022-07-26; was 71.6% from May 2011)
codes.note: The 71.6% figure in the task brief is the superseded 2011 value.

codes.name: Brewers Association Marketing and Advertising Code
codes.threshold: 'Advertising and marketing materials should only be placed in media where at least 73.6% of the audience is expected to be of legal drinking age.' (amended July 2022)

codes.name: DISCUS Code of Responsible Practices for Beverage Alcohol Advertising and Marketing
codes.threshold: 73.8% of audience reasonably expected to be 21+ (media placement, Section 2A.1) and 73.8% of attendees for fixed ads at venues (2A.2); since 2023-05-25, previously 71.6%
codes.note: Also bans college-campus marketing (2A.3) and states demographics alone are NOT sufficient for podcasts/apps - directly relevant to podcast properties. Applies to DISCUS members' beer and wine brands too.

codes.name: American Gaming Association Responsible Marketing Code for Sports Wagering
codes.threshold: 'only where at least 73.6 percent of the audience is reasonably expected to be 21 years or older' + no entertainers/athletes/influencers/music appealing primarily to under-21s; no college partnerships
codes.note: Text 'Updated: March 28, 2023'; covers sportsbooks, not DFS (PrizePicks) or prediction markets (Kalshi).
